items.title: Titanic survivor’s engagement ring sells for £150,000 at auction
items.summary: A diamond ring that belonged to one of the most famous survivors of the Titanic’s sinking has fetched £150,000 at auction.

items.title: Divulapitiya e-waste facility’s licence suspended after fire
items.summary: The environmental licence of an electronic waste processing facility in Wewagedara, Divulapitiya, has been temporarily suspended following a fire that broke out at the premises on November 16.

items.title: New draft deal aims to avert collapse of talks at climate summit
items.summary: Talks were set to resume at the UN COP31 summit on Sunday for a second day of overtime as countries struggled to reach a new global climate deal.

items.title: Doctors to launch two-hour island-wide trade union action tomorrow
items.summary: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) will launch a two-hour island-wide trade union action tomorrow (23), protesting the failure of the 2027 Budget to address doctors’ longstanding grievances.

items.title: Teachers, principals to launch island-wide strike on November 30
items.summary: Several teachers’ and principals’ trade unions have decided to launch an island-wide one-day strike on November 30, accusing the Government of failing to address their longstanding grievances through the 2027 Budget.

items.title: Workers’ protests planned for tomorrow, strikes on November 30
items.summary: The Workers’ Struggle Centre has announced plans to hold protests in front of government institutions and workplaces tomorrow (23), followed by sector-based strikes on November 30.

items.title: 21 University of Jaffna students remanded over clash
items.summary: Twenty-one students arrested in connection with a clash between two groups at the Faculty of Commerce and Management of the University of Jaffna have been remanded until November 26.

items.title: Six DIGs transferred
items.summary: Six Deputy Inspectors General of Police (DIGs) have been transferred with immediate effect by Inspector General of Police (IGP) Priyantha Weerasooriya, subject to the approval of the National Police Commission.

items.title: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as Iran tightens grip on shipping
items.summary: British maritime authorities have reported two incidents involving tankers struck by unidentified projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz, as Iran continues to restrict shipping through the vital waterway.

items.title: SJB MP questions Namal Rajapaksa’s continued remand, cites Bail Act
items.summary: SJB MP Chithral Fernando has questioned the continued remand of Opposition MP Namal Rajapaksa, arguing that the Bail Act No. 30 of 1997 establishes the granting of bail as the rule and its refusal as the exception.
